A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniRec-0.1B and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices. The appendix content is identical apart from pagination, supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original recognition experiments, HST/SDT ablations, inference timings and qualitative results in Tables 2–5 and Figures 4–11.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments in Tables 3–6 and Figures 4–11, and adds a model-scaling analysis in Figure 1(b).

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the FocalNet encoder, six-layer decoder, hierarchical supervision, semantic-decoupled tokenizer, cross-entropy objective and inference processing. The redrawn architecture diagram and scaling discussion do not establish a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Documented training and evaluation coverage remains UniRec40M, UniRec-Bench and OmniDocBench with the same languages, levels and domains. v2's new dataset-comparison table describes prior datasets without establishing their experimental use. Table recognition was already evaluated within the full-page parsing comparisons.

E2.justification: Corresponding recognition, document-parsing and timing tables retain identical comparator membership. Newly cited works such as Dolphin-v2 and DocHumming are not added to these evaluations. Figure 1(b) identifies parameter scales without specifying additional comparator methods.

E3.justification: Figure 1(b) adds a reported model-size sweep measuring recognition performance and latency. Existing training settings, benchmark partitions, metrics and timing procedures remain unchanged. Architectures and experimental controls for the new sweep are unspecified.

E4.justification: Figure 1(b) introduces a distinct cross-task capacity analysis investigating recognition saturation and the accuracy–latency tradeoff, substantially extending the analysis beyond component ablations and recognition examples. The HST/SDT ablations and all appendix case studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars for its results. The new scaling curves do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds scaling curves reporting text/formula saturation near 0.1B parameters, continuing table-performance gains and increasing latency, plus finer timing labels in Figure 1(d). Existing benchmark, ablation and timing values match exactly between v1 Tables 2–5 and v2 Tables 3–6; appendix results also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The model equations, token definitions and loss formulation are unchanged. The added 'scaling law analysis' is an empirical plot and interpretation, without a new mathematical law, derivation, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction adds the claim that text/formula recognition saturates around 0.1B parameters while tables benefit from larger models, strengthening the rationale for task specialization. It also explicitly asserts that named competing systems lack HST/SDT designs. The principal dataset, method and speedup contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 attributes continued table-recognition gains to greater task complexity and interprets differing scaling behavior as support for dividing recognition tasks between models. Existing explanations of component benefits and appendix limitations, including superscript/subscript failures in Figure 9, are retained.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 removes explicit arXiv, Wikipedia and PyMuPDF documentation links provided in v1. The OpenOCR code/dataset link, implementation settings, hardware and training-time disclosures remain unchanged. No reproducible setup is supplied for the new scaling analysis.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds dedicated training-data positioning, supported by a systematic comparison of dataset tasks, annotation levels, languages and sizes in new Table 1. This substantially expands the justification for UniRec40M's contribution. Additional literature includes Union14M-L, BCTR, Infinity-Doc, DocHumming and Dolphin-v2.

P1.justification: The introduction is locally rewritten around scaling and task specialization, related-work subsection headings become paragraph headings, and a training-data discussion and acknowledgements are added. Other sections receive limited wording corrections; the overall organization remains stable.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a full-width four-panel display, adding scaling curves and replacing timing pie charts with stacked bars. Figure 3 is substantially rearranged into a horizontal diagram. v2 also adds the dataset-comparison table and reformats existing table headers and placement; appendix displays are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The expanded dataset comparison and clearer architecture and timing graphics modestly improve context and readability. The new scaling analysis offers additional motivation, but unspecified models and experimental controls limit support for its broad saturation claim. With the method, established benchmark results and appendix evidence preserved, the net improvement is limited.
